 Oral Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI) This appeal is filed by the petitioner/appellant being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Bailhongal ('Tribunal' for short) vide judgment and award dated 18.02.2021 passed in MVC No. 1070 of 2017.

2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
2.1.
The petitioner met with an accident on 20.11.2016 and sustained grievous injuries.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-25/EG-5147.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries..
The charge sheet was filed against the rider of the motorcycle.

The petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before the Tribunal seeking compensation on account of the injuries sustained in the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3581 HC-KAR road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
2.2. A notice was issued to the owner of the motorcycle.

Despite the service of notice,
he remained unrepresented and was placed ex-parte before the Tribunal.

2.3. Respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed the statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of accident.
Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition.
2.4. The Tribunal, based on the rival pleadings of the parties, framed the relevant issues.

2.5. The petitioner, to substantiate his case, examined his next friend/wife as PW1,
examined the Doctor as PW2 and marked 24 documents as Exs.P1 to P24.
The Insurance Company has neither led any oral nor documentary evidence.

The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part vide judgment dated 18.02.2021 and awarded a compensation of 4,78,990/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the petition till its realisation and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest.

3. The petitioner, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
4. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

3 5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

To prove that the petitioner has suffered a permanent disability to the extent of 30%,
he has examined the Doctor as PW2, who has deposed that the petitioner has suffered a NC:
2026:KHC-D:3581 HC-KAR permanent disability to the extent of 30%, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 25% to the whole body, which is on the lower side.

He further submits that,
the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is also on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and do not call for any interference at the hands of this Court.

Hence, he prays to dismiss the appeal.
7.
Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
8. The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.

9. It is undisputed that the petitioner met with an accident, sustained grievous injuries, and the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3581 HC-KAR offending motorcycle.
The charge sheet is filed against the rider of the offending motorcycle.

The Tribunal, placing a reliance on the charge sheet at Ex.P7, has rightly recorded a finding that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle Reg.
Quantum

of compensation:
10.
It is the case of the petitioner that he was doing bar bending work prior to the accident and was earning 12,000/- per month.
The petitioner was aged about 36 years as of the date of accident.
After the accident, the petitioner has stopped working.
The petitionerhas examined the Doctor, who has issued the disability certificate at Ex.P24.
The Doctor has opined that there is an impairment of physical and intellectual function amounting to 25 to 30%.
The Tribunal, considering the evidence of PW2, has assessed the disability at 25% to the whole body, which is just and proper.
The petitioner, to prove the income, has not produced any income proof.

In the absence of income proof,
the Tribunal could have assessed the notional income NC: 2026:KHC-D:3581 HC-KAR as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority ('KSLSA' for short).
The Tribunal has assessed the monthly income at 8,000/-, which is on the lower side.

As the accident is of 2016,
the notional income has to be assessed at 8,750/- per month, as per the schedule issued by the KSLSA.

The applicable multiplier to the age group of the petitioner is '15' as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another1.
